results.construction: Circle centre M=(0,0), radius 5. Drag one end to (3,4) and the other to (-4,3)... both lie on the circle (9+16=25, 16+9=25). The segment joins two points on the circle and does not pass through the centre, so it is a chord. (Or (-5,0) to (3,4).)

predicates.why: It fires when one or both ends are off the circle, for example a segment that stops inside or runs past the circle. That is what a student holding the misconception 'a chord is any line across the circle' would build. The can_emit table lists it for the chord element.

results.construction: With M at the origin (centre), drag one end to (5,0) and the other to (-5,0). Both ends are on the circle of radius 5 and the segment passes through M, so it is a chord through the centre, with length 10.

predicates.why: It fires when the segment has both ends on the circle but misses M. A student who thinks any long chord is a diameter would build exactly that. The can_emit table lists it for diameter.

The can_emit table lists it for diameter, so it can fire. But a student with the 'chord endpoints off circle' misconception is thinking of chords that stop short or run past the circle. For a diameter, a segment with an end off the circle is more likely imprecise dragging, or a student who has drawn a line through the centre and not stopped it at the circle. It would mostly fire for those reasons and not for the chord misconception, so the diagnosis is not safe.

results.construction: Drag one end to the centre M (say M=(0,0)) and the other end to a point on the circle, e.g. (5,0). The segment from (0,0) to (5,0) has length 5, starts at the centre and ends on the circle.

predicates.why: Fires when both ends are on the circle (not at the centre) for a radius question. A student who thinks any segment inside the circle is a radius would build this. It is listed for radius.
Fires when one end is at the centre and the other is inside the circle, not on it. That is what a student who treats a radius as a direction of any length would build. It is listed for radius.

results.construction: Take M=(0,0), radius 5. Drag one end to (5,-3) and the other to (5,4) (both on the vertical line x=5). The segment's line is perpendicular to radius MP at P=(5,0) and touches the circle exactly once, at (5,0). The line x=5 is at distance 5 from M, so it is tangent. The instrument checks the property, so the segment must lie on the tangent line and may extend past the point of contact.

predicates.why: The tangent case lists this predicate. It fires when the line crosses the circle twice. A student who reads 'tangent' as any line touching or crossing the circle would draw this.

The tangent case lists this predicate, and it fires when the line misses the circle. A student who draws a line near the circle without touching it could have several reasons, such as imprecise dragging or a sloppy tangent point. The misconception 'tangent need not touch' is only one of them, so I mark it false.
